newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel economic officials extend talks to Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel economic officials extend talks to Tuesday.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel will continue talks on the government budget deficit on Tuesday, the Treasury said on Monday.
No decisions have been taken since the three began the series of meetings on Sunday.
Treasury officials said the government's domestic budget deficit in first quarter 1997 totalled 503 million shekels. The Treasury had forecast that the budget would be balanced in the first quarter.
The central bank has urged the government to cut the 1997 budget to keep the deficit within the target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
Pessimists among analysts say the government will miss the target by 0.8 percent of GDP or three to four billion shekels.
At Monday's meeting, Frenkel said lowering interest rates would not solve the problem of Israel's economic slowdown, sources present at the meeting said.
The Bank of Israel has refused to link a reduction in interest rates to a cut in the budget.
